package agecorpus

import (
	"context"
	"math"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// The text on the right of every case below was captured from apache/age
// 1.7.0 and cross-checked byte-for-byte against what pgx v5 scans
// (gqlc-35yu.5, corpus sections C1-C11). These bytes are what the
// helpers under test will actually be handed.
//
// This file is compiled in a throwaway module whose go.mod requires
// nothing, run with GOPROXY=off so that a corpus run cannot reach the
// network (see corpus_test.go). testify is therefore unavailable, and
// the repo's require/table-driven rule is suspended here of necessity:
// what these tests may use is the standard library and the emitted
// helpers, nothing else.

func TestAgtypeString(t *testing.T) {
	accepts := map[string]string{
		`"plain"`:            "plain",
		`""`:                 "",
		`"has \"quote\""`:    `has "quote"`,
		`"back\\slash"`:      `back\slash`,
		`"tab\there"`:        "tab\there",
		`"new\nline"`:        "new\nline",
		`"café ☕"`:           "café ☕",
		`"1.5"`:              "1.5",
		`"null"`:             "null",
		`"a$$, $1) AS (v)"`:  "a$$, $1) AS (v)",
		`"é"`:           "é",
	}
	// Subtests rather than a plain loop: corpusSubtests, in the parent
	// module that assembles this one, pins how many of these report a pass,
	// so a case added or dropped here has to be counted there too.
	for raw, want := range accepts {
		t.Run(raw, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := agtypeString([]byte(raw))
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("agtypeString(%s) = error %v, want %q", raw, err, want)
				return
			}
			if got != want {
				t.Errorf("agtypeString(%s) = %q, want %q", raw, got, want)
			}
		})
	}

	// Every other agtype shape. A projection that resolved to a string
	// and arrives as one of these is a mis-shaped result, and taking it
	// would hand the caller a plausible value built from the wrong thing.
	for _, raw := range []string{
		``,
		`plain`,
		`"unterminated`,
		`42`,
		`1.5`,
		`true`,
		`null`,
		`NaN`,
		`Infinity`,
		`1.5::numeric`,
		`[1, "a"]`,
		`{"a": 1}`,
		`"Alice"::vertex`,
		`{"id": 844424930131969, "label": "Person", "properties": {"name": "Alice"}}::vertex`,
		`"a" "b"`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeString([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeString(%s) = %q, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestAgtypeBool(t *testing.T) {
	for raw, want := range map[string]bool{`true`: true, `false`: false} {
		got, err := agtypeBool([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeBool(%s) = error %v, want %v", raw, err, want)
			continue
		}
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("agtypeBool(%s) = %v, want %v", raw, got, want)
		}
	}

	// The two spellings above are agtype's whole boolean vocabulary. The
	// abbreviated and numeric forms belong to other parsers.
	for _, raw := range []string{
		``,
		`t`,
		`f`,
		`T`,
		`TRUE`,
		`True`,
		`FALSE`,
		`1`,
		`0`,
		`yes`,
		`"true"`,
		`null`,
		` true`,
		`true `,
		`[true]`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeBool([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeBool(%s) = %v, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestAgtypeInt64(t *testing.T) {
	accepts := map[string]int64{
		`0`:                     0,
		`42`:                    42,
		`-42`:                   -42,
		`9223372036854775807`:   math.MaxInt64,
		`-9223372036854775808`:  math.MinInt64,
		`253402300799000000`:    253402300799000000,
		`-2208988800000000`:     -2208988800000000,
		`3::numeric`:            3,
		`-3::numeric`:           -3,
	}
	for raw, want := range accepts {
		got, err := agtypeInt64([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInt64(%s) = error %v, want %d", raw, err, want)
			continue
		}
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInt64(%s) = %d, want %d", raw, got, want)
		}
	}

	// 9223372036854775808 is the value AGE itself turns into a float on
	// overflow, so it arrives as 9.223372036854776e+18 — either spelling
	// is out of an int64 column's range and neither may be truncated
	// into one.
	for _, raw := range []string{
		``,
		`1.5`,
		`1.0`,
		`1.5::numeric`,
		`9223372036854775808`,
		`-9223372036854775809`,
		`9.223372036854776e+18`,
		`1e100`,
		`NaN`,
		`Infinity`,
		`-Infinity`,
		`"42"`,
		`true`,
		`null`,
		`[42]`,
		`42 43`,
		`0x2a`,
		`4_2`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeInt64([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInt64(%s) = %d, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestAgtypeFloat64(t *testing.T) {
	accepts := map[string]float64{
		`1.5`:                  1.5,
		`-1.5`:                 -1.5,
		`1.0`:                  1,
		`0.30000000000000004`:  0.30000000000000004,
		`0.3333333333333333`:   0.3333333333333333,
		`1e+100`:               1e100,
		`42`:                   42,
		`-42`:                  -42,
		`9223372036854775807`:  9223372036854775807,
		`1.5::numeric`:         1.5,
		`9.223372036854776e+18`: 9.223372036854776e+18,
	}
	for raw, want := range accepts {
		got, err := agtypeFloat64([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeFloat64(%s) = error %v, want %v", raw, err, want)
			continue
		}
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("agtypeFloat64(%s) = %v, want %v", raw, got, want)
		}
	}

	// NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are agtype's float vocabulary and JSON
	// has no spelling for any of them, which is why the float parser
	// reads these bytes and the JSON decoder does not.
	nan, err := agtypeFloat64([]byte(`NaN`))
	if err != nil || !math.IsNaN(nan) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeFloat64(NaN) = %v, %v, want NaN", nan, err)
	}
	for raw, sign := range map[string]int{`Infinity`: 1, `-Infinity`: -1} {
		got, err := agtypeFloat64([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil || !math.IsInf(got, sign) {
			t.Errorf("agtypeFloat64(%s) = %v, %v, want %+d infinity", raw, got, err, sign)
		}
	}

	// -0.0 is a value AGE emits and it is not 0.0: a caller comparing
	// signs sees the difference.
	neg, err := agtypeFloat64([]byte(`-0.0`))
	if err != nil || !math.Signbit(neg) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeFloat64(-0.0) = %v, %v, want negative zero", neg, err)
	}

	for _, raw := range []string{
		``,
		`"1.5"`,
		`true`,
		`null`,
		`[1.5]`,
		`{"a": 1.5}`,
		`1.5 2.5`,
		`1.5::vertex`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeFloat64([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeFloat64(%s) = %v, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

// The vertex and edge texts below were captured the same way the scalars
// above were, by writing the value through cypher() and reading back what
// pgx scans (gqlc-35yu.5 C7-C9). Two properties of the wire form the
// decoders have to survive are visible in them: jsonb orders an object's
// keys by length and then lexicographically, so a property's position is
// not the schema's or the author's, and a null property arrives as no key
// at all rather than as a key holding null.
const (
	alice  = `{"id": 844424930131969, "label": "Person", "properties": {"id": 1, "rank": 3, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex`
	bob    = `{"id": 844424930131970, "label": "Person", "properties": {"id": 2, "rank": 4, "name": "Bob", "score": 1.0, "weight": 0.5, "active": false, "middleName": "Q"}}::vertex`
	marker = `{"id": 1407374883553281, "label": "Marker", "properties": {}}::vertex`
	actedIn = `{"id": 1125899906842625, "label": "ACTED_IN", "end_id": 844424930131970, "start_id": 844424930131969, "properties": {"since": 2019}}::edge`

	// AGE stores whatever a writer wrote, so a vertex carrying the KEY
	// label a query matched on may hold properties the schema never
	// declared, of shapes it never declares. Reaching `name` here means
	// stepping over a list and a nested map, and the value itself holds a
	// comma, a closing brace, an escaped quote and a colon.
	tricky = `{"id": 1688849860263937, "label": "Tricky", "properties": {"big": 1.5, "huge": 9223372036854775807, "name": "a, b} c\": {d", "tags": ["x", "y"], "nested": {"x": 1, "y": [1, 2]}}}::vertex`
)

func TestDecodeVertex(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodePerson([]byte(alice))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodePerson(alice) = error %v", err)
	}
	want := Person{Active: true, Id: 1, Name: "Alice", Rank: 3, Score: 9.5}
	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("decodePerson(alice) = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}

	// A property AGE did not send is the schema's null, and the pointer
	// is what carries that to the caller: a zero value would report
	// "no middle name" as a middle name of "".
	if got.MiddleName != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodePerson(alice).MiddleName = %q, want nil", *got.MiddleName)
	}
	if got.Weight != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodePerson(alice).Weight = %v, want nil", *got.Weight)
	}
}

func TestDecodeVertexReadsNullableProperties(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodePerson([]byte(bob))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodePerson(bob) = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.MiddleName == nil || *got.MiddleName != "Q" {
		t.Errorf("decodePerson(bob).MiddleName = %v, want a pointer to \"Q\"", got.MiddleName)
	}
	// FLOAT32 rides agtype's float64 and narrows at the field, so the
	// pointer has to address a float32 and not the carrier.
	if got.Weight == nil || *got.Weight != float32(0.5) {
		t.Errorf("decodePerson(bob).Weight = %v, want a pointer to 0.5", got.Weight)
	}
	if got.Rank != 4 {
		t.Errorf("decodePerson(bob).Rank = %d, want 4", got.Rank)
	}
}

func TestDecodeVertexStepsOverStructuredProperties(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeTricky([]byte(tricky))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeTricky = error %v", err)
	}
	const want = `a, b} c": {d`
	if got.Name != want {
		t.Errorf("decodeTricky().Name = %q, want %q", got.Name, want)
	}
}

func TestDecodeZeroPropertyVertex(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := decodeMarker([]byte(marker)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeMarker(marker) = error %v", err)
	}
	// The label is the whole of a zero-property entity's identity, so it
	// is the whole of what its decoder can check.
	if got, err := decodeMarker([]byte(alice)); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeMarker(alice) = %+v, want an error", got)
	}
}

// The list and open-shape texts below were captured the same way the
// scalars and entities above were, by writing the values through
// cypher() and reading back what pgx scans (apache/age 1.7.0). Three
// things visible in them shape the decoders: AGE separates elements with
// a comma and a space, a string element is JSON-escaped so a delimiter
// inside one ends nothing, and a list-valued property that is null
// arrives as no key at all — listyNulls carries no "depths".
const (
	listy      = `{"id": 844424930131969, "label": "Listy", "properties": {"tags": ["x", "y"], "ranks": [1, -2, 2147483647], "depths": [0.5, 1.5], "matrix": [[1], [2, 3]]}}::vertex`
	listyEmpty = `{"id": 844424930131970, "label": "Listy", "properties": {"tags": [], "ranks": [], "depths": [], "matrix": [[]]}}::vertex`
	listyNulls = `{"id": 844424930131971, "label": "Listy", "properties": {"tags": ["a, b] c\": {d", ""], "ranks": [0], "matrix": []}}::vertex`

	anyInt = `{"id": 1125899906842625, "label": "Anything", "properties": {"other": "text", "payload": 42}}::vertex`
	// anyTag holds the second spelling of the same declared width, ANY
	// PROPERTY VALUE, beside the first. Both properties are here at once
	// so what the assertion compares is the two spellings on one vertex.
	anyTag = `{"id": 1125899906842628, "label": "Anything", "properties": {"payload": 42, "tag": {"a": 1}}}::vertex`
	anyMap = `{"id": 1125899906842626, "label": "Anything", "properties": {"payload": {"a": 1, "b": [true, null, "z"], "c": {"d": 1.5}}}}::vertex`
	anyList = `{"id": 1125899906842627, "label": "Anything", "properties": {"payload": [1, "two", 3.5, true, null, [1, 2], {"k": "v"}]}}::vertex`
)

func TestAgtypeListOfString(t *testing.T) {
	accepts := map[string][]string{
		`["x", "y"]`: {"x", "y"},
		// The want here is an empty slice and not nil, and slicesEqual holds
		// the difference: AGE sent a list, so what reaches the caller has to
		// be one.
		`[]`:                     {},
		`["a"]`:                  {"a"},
		`[""]`:                   {""},
		// A delimiter inside an element ends nothing: the element is
		// stepped over whole before the split looks for the next comma.
		`["a, b] c\": {d", ""]`: {`a, b] c": {d`, ""},
	}
	for raw, want := range accepts {
		got, err := agtypeListOfString([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeListOfString(%s) = error %v, want %v", raw, err, want)
			continue
		}
		if !slicesEqual(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("agtypeListOfString(%s) = %#v, want %#v", raw, got, want)
		}
	}

	// Every shape that is not an agtype list. Taking any of them would
	// hand the caller a slice built from something the graph does not
	// hold as one.
	for _, raw := range []string{
		``,
		`null`,
		`42`,
		`"x"`,
		`true`,
		`{"a": 1}`,
		`[1, 2`,
		`1, 2]`,
		`["x"] ["y"]`,
		`{"id": 1, "label": "Listy", "properties": {}}::vertex`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeListOfString([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeListOfString(%s) = %#v, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

// AGE stores whatever a writer wrote, so a property the schema declares
// LIST<STRING> can arrive holding an element of any other agtype shape —
// a number, a boolean, a nested structure, or the null that a list, unlike
// a property, does carry inline. An element decoder that took one would
// build a []string out of something else.
func TestAgtypeListRefusesAnElementOfTheWrongScalar(t *testing.T) {
	for _, raw := range []string{
		`[42]`,
		`["x", 42]`,
		`["a", null, "c"]`,
		`[true]`,
		`[["x"]]`,
		`[{"a": 1}]`,
		`[1.5]`,
		`[x]`,
		`[, "x"]`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeListOfString([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeListOfString(%s) = %#v, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
	for _, raw := range []string{`["1"]`, `[1.5]`, `[true]`, `[null]`, `[[1]]`} {
		if got, err := agtypeListOfInt32([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeListOfInt32(%s) = %#v, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

// A nested list decodes through the decoder emitted for its own element
// type, so the depth the schema declared is the depth the walk goes to
// and an element one short of it fails rather than flattening.
func TestAgtypeNestedList(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := agtypeListOfListOfInt64([]byte(`[[1], [2, 3]]`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("agtypeListOfListOfInt64([[1], [2, 3]]) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 2 || !slicesEqual(got[0], []int64{1}) || !slicesEqual(got[1], []int64{2, 3}) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeListOfListOfInt64([[1], [2, 3]]) = %#v, want [[1] [2 3]]", got)
	}

	// An empty outer list and a list holding one empty inner list are
	// different values, and the wire spells them differently.
	outer, err := agtypeListOfListOfInt64([]byte(`[]`))
	if err != nil || outer == nil || len(outer) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("agtypeListOfListOfInt64([]) = %#v, %v, want an empty slice", outer, err)
	}
	inner, err := agtypeListOfListOfInt64([]byte(`[[]]`))
	if err != nil || len(inner) != 1 || inner[0] == nil || len(inner[0]) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("agtypeListOfListOfInt64([[]]) = %#v, %v, want one empty slice", inner, err)
	}

	for _, raw := range []string{`[1]`, `[[1], 2]`, `[[1], null]`, `[["a"]]`, `[[[1]]]`} {
		if bad, err := agtypeListOfListOfInt64([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeListOfListOfInt64(%s) = %#v, want an error", raw, bad)
		}
	}
}

// A narrow element width rides the agtype scalar its carrier is and
// converts per element, so the slice holds the width the schema declared
// and not the carrier's.
func TestAgtypeListOfNarrowElementWidth(t *testing.T) {
	ranks, err := agtypeListOfInt32([]byte(`[1, -2, 2147483647]`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("agtypeListOfInt32 = error %v", err)
	}
	if !slicesEqual(ranks, []int32{1, -2, 2147483647}) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeListOfInt32([1, -2, 2147483647]) = %#v", ranks)
	}

	depths, err := agtypeListOfFloat32([]byte(`[0.5, 1.5]`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("agtypeListOfFloat32 = error %v", err)
	}
	if !slicesEqual(depths, []float32{0.5, 1.5}) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeListOfFloat32([0.5, 1.5]) = %#v", depths)
	}
}

func TestDecodeVertexWithListProperties(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeListy([]byte(listy))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(listy) = error %v", err)
	}
	if !slicesEqual(got.Tags, []string{"x", "y"}) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listy).Tags = %#v", got.Tags)
	}
	if !slicesEqual(got.Ranks, []int32{1, -2, 2147483647}) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listy).Ranks = %#v", got.Ranks)
	}
	if len(got.Matrix) != 2 || !slicesEqual(got.Matrix[0], []int64{1}) || !slicesEqual(got.Matrix[1], []int64{2, 3}) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listy).Matrix = %#v", got.Matrix)
	}
	if got.Depths == nil || !slicesEqual(*got.Depths, []float32{0.5, 1.5}) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listy).Depths = %#v", got.Depths)
	}

	empty, err := decodeListy([]byte(listyEmpty))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(listyEmpty) = error %v", err)
	}
	// An empty list is a value the graph holds, and it is not the absence a
	// nullable property reports. Both halves are checked: the pointer is
	// non-nil, and the slice it addresses is an empty slice rather than the
	// nil one an absent property would reach the caller as.
	if empty.Depths == nil || *empty.Depths == nil || len(*empty.Depths) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listyEmpty).Depths = %#v, want a pointer to an empty slice", empty.Depths)
	}
	if empty.Tags == nil || len(empty.Tags) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listyEmpty).Tags = %#v, want an empty slice", empty.Tags)
	}
	if empty.Ranks == nil || len(empty.Ranks) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listyEmpty).Ranks = %#v, want an empty slice", empty.Ranks)
	}
	if len(empty.Matrix) != 1 || empty.Matrix[0] == nil || len(empty.Matrix[0]) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listyEmpty).Matrix = %#v, want one empty slice", empty.Matrix)
	}

	// AGE drops a property whose value is null, so a nullable list that
	// is null arrives as no key — the same absence a nullable scalar
	// arrives as.
	nulls, err := decodeListy([]byte(listyNulls))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(listyNulls) = error %v", err)
	}
	if nulls.Depths != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listyNulls).Depths = %#v, want nil", nulls.Depths)
	}
	if !slicesEqual(nulls.Tags, []string{`a, b] c": {d`, ""}) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(listyNulls).Tags = %#v", nulls.Tags)
	}
}

// A property of no declared shape decodes through agtype's own value
// vocabulary rather than through one width, so what the caller gets is
// the shape the graph holds: agtype's integer and float land on Go's
// int64 and float64, its list on []any and its map on map[string]any,
// and the null it carries inline lands on nil.
func TestAgtypeValue(t *testing.T) {
	scalars := map[string]any{
		`42`:           int64(42),
		`-42`:          int64(-42),
		`3::numeric`:   int64(3),
		`1.5`:          1.5,
		`1.0`:          1.0,
		`1e+100`:       1e100,
		`1.5::numeric`: 1.5,
		`"two"`:        "two",
		`""`:           "",
		`"42"`:         "42",
		`true`:         true,
		`false`:        false,
		`null`:         nil,
	}
	for raw, want := range scalars {
		got, err := agtypeValue([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeValue(%s) = error %v, want %v", raw, err, want)
			continue
		}
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("agtypeValue(%s) = %#v, want %#v", raw, got, want)
		}
	}

	// A value out of int64's range is one AGE itself turned into a float,
	// and it reaches the caller as the float it is rather than failing or
	// truncating.
	big, err := agtypeValue([]byte(`9.223372036854776e+18`))
	if err != nil || big != 9.223372036854776e18 {
		t.Errorf("agtypeValue(9.223372036854776e+18) = %#v, %v", big, err)
	}
	nan, err := agtypeValue([]byte(`NaN`))
	if f, ok := nan.(float64); err != nil || !ok || !math.IsNaN(f) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeValue(NaN) = %#v, %v, want NaN", nan, err)
	}

	list, err := agtypeValue([]byte(`[1, "two", 3.5, true, null, [1, 2], {"k": "v"}]`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("agtypeValue(list) = error %v", err)
	}
	xs, ok := list.([]any)
	if !ok || len(xs) != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("agtypeValue(list) = %#v, want a []any of 7", list)
	}
	if xs[0] != int64(1) || xs[1] != "two" || xs[2] != 3.5 || xs[3] != true || xs[4] != nil {
		t.Errorf("agtypeValue(list) = %#v", xs)
	}
	if nested, ok := xs[5].([]any); !ok || len(nested) != 2 || nested[0] != int64(1) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeValue(list)[5] = %#v, want []any{1, 2}", xs[5])
	}
	if member, ok := xs[6].(map[string]any); !ok || member["k"] != "v" {
		t.Errorf("agtypeValue(list)[6] = %#v, want map[k:v]", xs[6])
	}

	object, err := agtypeValue([]byte(`{"a": 1, "b": [true, null, "z"], "c": {"d": 1.5}}`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("agtypeValue(map) = error %v", err)
	}
	m, ok := object.(map[string]any)
	if !ok || len(m) != 3 || m["a"] != int64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("agtypeValue(map) = %#v", object)
	}
	if b, ok := m["b"].([]any); !ok || len(b) != 3 || b[0] != true || b[1] != nil || b[2] != "z" {
		t.Errorf("agtypeValue(map)[b] = %#v", m["b"])
	}
	if c, ok := m["c"].(map[string]any); !ok || c["d"] != 1.5 {
		t.Errorf("agtypeValue(map)[c] = %#v", m["c"])
	}

	// Text outside agtype's value vocabulary is not a value of unknown
	// shape, it is not a value: reading it as one would put a fabricated
	// Go value in a caller's hands.
	for _, raw := range []string{
		``,
		`  `,
		`plain`,
		`"unterminated`,
		`[1, 2`,
		`{"a": 1`,
		`{"a"}`,
		`1 2`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeValue([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeValue(%s) = %#v, want an error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestDecodeVertexWithAnyProperty(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeAnything([]byte(anyInt))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(anyInt) = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.Payload != int64(42) {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(anyInt).Payload = %#v, want int64(42)", got.Payload)
	}
	// The property the schema declares nullable is absent here, and the
	// pointer is what carries that: a non-nil pointer to a nil any would
	// say the graph holds an untyped null.
	if got.Maybe != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(anyInt).Maybe = %#v, want nil", got.Maybe)
	}

	object, err := decodeAnything([]byte(anyMap))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(anyMap) = error %v", err)
	}
	if m, ok := object.Payload.(map[string]any); !ok || m["a"] != int64(1) {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(anyMap).Payload = %#v", object.Payload)
	}

	list, err := decodeAnything([]byte(anyList))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(anyList) = error %v", err)
	}
	if xs, ok := list.Payload.([]any); !ok || len(xs) != 7 {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(anyList).Payload = %#v", list.Payload)
	}

	// ANY PROPERTY VALUE is a second spelling of the width payload is
	// declared with -- internal/schema/gql/propertytype.go maps "ANY
	// VALUE", "ANY", "PROPERTY VALUE" and "ANY PROPERTY VALUE" all onto
	// graph.TypeAnyPropertyValue -- so the emission is expected to give
	// tag the same decode payload gets. That expectation had no row on
	// any target until bd gqlc-v7vu: the schema fixture pinned the
	// spelling as golden bytes only, and -update blesses golden bytes
	// away. This runs it.
	tagged, err := decodeAnything([]byte(anyTag))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(anyTag) = error %v", err)
	}
	if tagged.Tag == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(anyTag).Tag = nil, want a pointer to the held value")
	}
	if m, ok := (*tagged.Tag).(map[string]any); !ok || m["a"] != int64(1) {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(anyTag).Tag points at %#v, want map[a:1]", *tagged.Tag)
	}
	// The absent half: anyInt declares no tag, and the pointer is what
	// carries that, the same way Maybe carries it one property over.
	if got.Tag != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(anyInt).Tag = %#v, want nil", got.Tag)
	}
}

// slicesEqual is the corpus module's own comparison: the module requires
// nothing, so testify is unavailable and this is one line rather than a
// dependency. A nil slice and an empty one are not equal here: the graph
// holding an empty list and the graph holding nothing are different
// answers, and length alone cannot tell them apart.
func slicesEqual[T comparable](got, want []T) bool {
	if (got == nil) != (want == nil) {
		return false
	}
	if len(got) != len(want) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range got {
		if got[i] != want[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func TestDecodeEdge(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeACTEDIN([]byte(actedIn))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeACTEDIN = error %v", err)
	}
	if want := (ACTEDIN{Since: 2019}); got != want {
		t.Errorf("decodeACTEDIN = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
}

// A vertex and an edge are the same object but for the annotation, so the
// annotation is the only thing standing between an edge decoder and a
// vertex whose label happens to match. Both directions are checked.
func TestEntityDecodersRefuseTheOtherAnnotation(t *testing.T) {
	edgeShapedAsVertex := strings.Replace(actedIn, "::edge", "::vertex", 1)
	if got, err := decodeACTEDIN([]byte(edgeShapedAsVertex)); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeACTEDIN(vertex) = %+v, want an error", got)
	}
	vertexShapedAsEdge := strings.Replace(alice, "::vertex", "::edge", 1)
	if got, err := decodePerson([]byte(vertexShapedAsEdge)); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodePerson(edge) = %+v, want an error", got)
	}
}

// Every shape that is not the vertex the decoder was emitted for. A
// decoder that took any of these would hand the caller a struct built
// from something other than the entity its type names.
func TestDecodeVertexRefusesMisshapenText(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]string{
		"empty":                 ``,
		"agtype null":           `null`,
		"a bare scalar":         `42`,
		"a bare object":         `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": {"id": 1, "rank": 3, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}`,
		"the wrong label":       `{"id": 1, "label": "Movie", "properties": {"id": 1, "rank": 3, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex`,
		"no label":              `{"id": 1, "properties": {"id": 1, "rank": 3, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex`,
		"a non-string label":    `{"id": 1, "label": 7, "properties": {"id": 1, "rank": 3, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex`,
		"no properties":         `{"id": 1, "label": "Person"}::vertex`,
		"non-object properties": `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": [1, 2]}::vertex`,
		"a missing property":    `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": {"id": 1, "rank": 3, "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex`,
		"a property of the wrong shape": `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": {"id": 1, "rank": 3, "name": 42, "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex`,
		"an out-of-range property":      `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": {"id": 9.5, "rank": 3, "name": "Alice", "score": 9.5, "active": true}}::vertex`,
		"an unterminated string":        `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": {"name": "Alice}}::vertex`,
		"an unbalanced brace":           `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": {"name": "Alice"}::vertex`,
		"a member with no value":        `{"id": 1, "label": "Person", "properties": {"name"}}::vertex`,
		"the annotation alone":          `::vertex`,
	}
	for name, raw := range cases {
		if got, err := decodePerson([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: decodePerson(%s) = %+v, want an error", name, raw, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestAgtypeArgs(t *testing.T) {
	// The encoder's output is the whole of what AGE parses as the query's
	// parameter map, so a value carrying agtype's own delimiters has to
	// come back out inside the JSON string it went in as.
	cases := map[string]struct {
		args map[string]any
		want string
	}{
		"empty":     {map[string]any{}, `{}`},
		"scalars":   {map[string]any{"id": int64(1), "ok": true}, `{"id":1,"ok":true}`},
		"null":      {map[string]any{"minAge": (*int64)(nil)}, `{"minAge":null}`},
		"delimiter": {map[string]any{"n": `a$$, $1) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)`}, `{"n":"a$$, $1) AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)"}`},
		"quote":     {map[string]any{"n": `'; DROP TABLE canary; --`}, `{"n":"'; DROP TABLE canary; --"}`},
		"backslash": {map[string]any{"n": `back\slash`}, `{"n":"back\\slash"}`},
		"unicode":   {map[string]any{"n": "café"}, `{"n":"café"}`},
	}
	for name, tc := range cases {
		got, err := agtypeArgs(tc.args)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeArgs = error %v", name, err)
			continue
		}
		if got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeArgs = %s, want %s", name, got, tc.want)
		}
	}

	// A value the encoder cannot render must fail rather than produce
	// text AGE would read as something else.
	if got, err := agtypeArgs(map[string]any{"n": make(chan int)}); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("agtypeArgs(chan) = %s, want an error", got)
	}
}

// The graph name is the one value that reaches the server inside the
// statement text rather than bound to a placeholder, so the escaping is
// what keeps a name carrying SQL's or agtype's own delimiters a single
// literal. AGE refuses a quote or a backslash in a graph name of its own
// accord at create_graph; the two barriers stand independently and this
// pins the SQL-layer one. The tag rows carry both the first candidate
// and an escalated one, since the composed body has to bracket the query
// text either way.
func TestCypherStmtComposesOneStatement(t *testing.T) {
	const text = "MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.id = $id RETURN p.name"
	const record = "v0 ag_catalog.agtype"

	cases := map[string]struct {
		graph string
		tag   string
		want  string
	}{
		"plain":     {"people", "$gqlc$", `E'people'`},
		"quote":     {`o'brien`, "$gqlc$", `E'o\'brien'`},
		"backslash": {`back\slash`, "$gqlc$", `E'back\\slash'`},
		"both":      {`a\'b`, "$gqlc$", `E'a\\\'b'`},
		"statement break": {
			`x', $q$ $q$) AS (n ag_catalog.agtype); DROP TABLE victim; --`,
			"$gqlc$",
			`E'x\', $q$ $q$) AS (n ag_catalog.agtype); DROP TABLE victim; --'`,
		},
		"escalated tag": {"people", "$gqlc1$", `E'people'`},
	}
	for name, tc := range cases {
		got, err := (&Queries{graph: tc.graph}).cypherStmt(tc.tag, text, record)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: cypherStmt = error %v", name, err)
			continue
		}
		want := "SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher(" + tc.want + ", " + tc.tag + text + tc.tag + ", $1) AS (" + record + ")"
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("%s: cypherStmt =\n\t%s\nwant\n\t%s", name, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// A name the server would shorten produces no statement at all, so there
// is nothing for a caller to run against whichever graph the truncation
// would have landed on.
func TestCypherStmtRefusesAnOverlongName(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := (&Queries{graph: strings.Repeat("g", 64)}).cypherStmt("$gqlc$", "RETURN 1", "v0 ag_catalog.agtype")
	if err == nil {
		t.Errorf("cypherStmt = %s, want an error", got)
	}
	if got != "" {
		t.Errorf("cypherStmt returned %q alongside its error", got)
	}
}

// The TIMESTAMP encoding. agtype has no temporal value and AGE has no
// temporal function but timestamp(), which answers in MILLIseconds, so
// what an instant means on this wire is settled by the emitted helpers
// and by nothing else: a count of MICROseconds since the Unix epoch in
// the integer scalar, with the zone — when the graph carries one — in a
// separate property named <property>Offset holding SECONDS.
//
// These counts are not captured the way the scalars above are: no AGE
// build ever produced a temporal value to capture. They are computed
// from the encoding the spike settled (gqlc-35yu.5), and every row below
// is a different number under a different unit, a different epoch or a
// different zone rule — which is the whole reason to assert the numbers
// rather than the shape of the code that produces them.
//
// The rows are the values an encoding fails on rather than a comfortable
// middle: one before the epoch, so a count that cannot go negative
// breaks; the epoch itself; one carrying microseconds, so a coarser
// resolution loses them; and one at the far end of the range, so a unit
// off by a thousand overflows.
var instants = []struct {
	name   string
	micros int64
	at     time.Time
}{
	{"pre-epoch", -14182940000000, time.Date(1969, 7, 20, 20, 17, 40, 0, time.UTC)},
	{"the epoch", 0, time.Unix(0, 0).UTC()},
	{"sub-second", 1704112496123456, time.Date(2024, 1, 1, 12, 34, 56, 123456000, time.UTC)},
	{"year 9999", 253402300799999999, time.Date(9999, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, 999999000, time.UTC)},
}

// tehran is the sub-second instant above spelled in a zone 3.5 hours
// ahead. The same moment under two spellings has to encode to one count,
// which is what makes a range predicate over the stored property answer
// by instant and not by wall clock.
var tehran = time.Date(2024, 1, 1, 16, 4, 56, 123456000, time.FixedZone("", 12600))

func TestAgtypeInstantCountsMicrosecondsFromTheEpoch(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range instants {
		raw := strconv.FormatInt(tc.micros, 10)
		got, err := agtypeInstant([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeInstant(%s) = error %v", tc.name, raw, err)
			continue
		}
		if !got.Equal(tc.at) {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeInstant(%s) = %s, want %s", tc.name, raw, got.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), tc.at.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
		}
		// The count names an instant and no zone, so what comes back is
		// UTC — not the zone the host running this happens to be in.
		if got.Location() != time.UTC {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeInstant(%s) is in %s, want UTC", tc.name, raw, got.Location())
		}
	}

	// A count is the whole encoding, so every other spelling of a time —
	// the ISO text an author might expect, a float, a quoted count — is a
	// value this column cannot hold.
	for _, raw := range []string{
		``,
		`1.5`,
		`"1704112496123456"`,
		`"2024-01-01T12:34:56.123456Z"`,
		`null`,
		`true`,
		`[1704112496123456]`,
	} {
		if got, err := agtypeInstant([]byte(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInstant(%s) = %s, want an error", raw, got.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
		}
	}
}

// TestAgtypeInstantRefusesACountOutsideTheCalendar pins the bound on the
// stored count. gqlc's encode writes the micros, but the property it
// writes them to is an ordinary agtype integer on a vertex any writer can
// touch, so the count read back is whatever the graph holds — the same
// argument that bounds the offset sidecar, one property over.
//
// Taken unchecked, math.MaxInt64 microseconds decodes to a year near
// 294247 and is returned with no error. That is not a date any wire
// format beside this one spells: RFC 3339 has four year digits, and so
// does every timestamp text a SQL client prints. A caller who formats it
// gets a string no other system will read back.
//
// The admitted range is therefore the four-digit calendar, year 1 through
// year 9999 inclusive, which is exactly the range the corpus above spans:
// its far-end row, 253402300799999999, IS the upper bound, and its
// pre-epoch row sits well inside the lower one. Both edges are read here
// so the bound is a range and not a ceiling.
func TestAgtypeInstantRefusesACountOutsideTheCalendar(t *testing.T) {
	// The two edges themselves, which are admitted. The upper one is the
	// year-9999 row above; the lower is midnight at the start of year 1.
	for _, micros := range []int64{-62135596800000000, 253402300799999999} {
		raw := strconv.FormatInt(micros, 10)
		got, err := agtypeInstant([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInstant(%s) = error %v, want the instant read", raw, err)
			continue
		}
		if got.UnixMicro() != micros {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInstant(%s) = %s, whose count is %d", raw, got.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), got.UnixMicro())
		}
	}

	// One microsecond outside each edge, and the int64 extremes beyond
	// them. The one-microsecond rows are what a bound written with the
	// wrong comparison lets through; the extremes are what an absent
	// bound lets through.
	for _, micros := range []int64{
		-62135596800000001,
		253402300800000000,
		math.MaxInt64,
		math.MinInt64,
	} {
		raw := strconv.FormatInt(micros, 10)
		got, err := agtypeInstant([]byte(raw))
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInstant(%s) = %s, want an error", raw, got.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
			continue
		}
		// The count is the whole of what went wrong, so it has to be in
		// the message: a reader looking at a failed row has the property
		// name from the decoder that called this and nothing else.
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), raw) {
			t.Errorf("agtypeInstant(%s) = error %v, which does not name the count it read", raw, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestAgtypeMicrosEncodesTheInstantAndNotTheWallClock(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range instants {
		if got := agtypeMicros(tc.at); got != tc.micros {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeMicros(%s) = %d, want %d", tc.name, tc.at.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), got, tc.micros)
		}
	}

	// Encode and decode are one encoding read from either end, so a value
	// that survives one and not the other is a bug neither test sees
	// alone.
	for _, tc := range instants {
		back, err := agtypeInstant([]byte(strconv.FormatInt(agtypeMicros(tc.at), 10)))
		if err != nil || !back.Equal(tc.at) {
			t.Errorf("%s: round trip = %s, %v, want %s", tc.name, back.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), err, tc.at.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
		}
	}

	if got := agtypeMicros(tehran); got != instants[2].micros {
		t.Errorf("agtypeMicros(%s) = %d, want %d — the same moment in another zone is the same count",
			tehran.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), got, instants[2].micros)
	}
}

func TestAgtypeNullableMicrosCarriesAbsence(t *testing.T) {
	if got := agtypeNullableMicros(nil); got != nil {
		t.Errorf("agtypeNullableMicros(nil) = %d, want nil", *got)
	}
	for _, tc := range instants {
		at := tc.at
		got := agtypeNullableMicros(&at)
		if got == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeNullableMicros = nil, want %d", tc.name, tc.micros)
			continue
		}
		if *got != tc.micros {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeNullableMicros = %d, want %d", tc.name, *got, tc.micros)
		}
	}
}

func TestAgtypeZoneReadsAnOffsetInSeconds(t *testing.T) {
	at := instants[2].at

	// 12600 is +03:30 and -18000 is -05:00. Read as minutes instead of
	// seconds the first is 210 hours and the second 300 hours back, so a
	// unit confusion here cannot land on a plausible zone.
	cases := map[string]struct {
		raw    string
		offset int
	}{
		"utc":            {`0`, 0},
		"ahead":          {`12600`, 12600},
		"behind":         {`-18000`, -18000},
		"a whole degree": {`3600`, 3600},
	}
	for name, tc := range cases {
		got, err := agtypeZone(map[string][]byte{"occurredAtOffset": []byte(tc.raw)}, "occurredAtOffset", at)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeZone = error %v", name, err)
			continue
		}
		// The sidecar moves the zone and not the instant: a value stored
		// under one offset and read under another is the same moment.
		if !got.Equal(at) {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeZone moved the instant to %s, want %s", name, got.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), at.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
		}
		if _, off := got.Zone(); off != tc.offset {
			t.Errorf("%s: agtypeZone offset = %d seconds, want %d", name, off, tc.offset)
		}
	}

	// An absent sidecar is not a failure. The count is complete without
	// one, and gqlc's own write path never writes one — the sidecar is
	// there so a zone some other writer put in the graph survives a read.
	plain, err := agtypeZone(map[string][]byte{}, "occurredAtOffset", at)
	if err != nil {
		t.Errorf("agtypeZone with no sidecar = error %v", err)
	} else if plain.Location() != time.UTC || !plain.Equal(at) {
		t.Errorf("agtypeZone with no sidecar = %s in %s, want %s in UTC",
			plain.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), plain.Location(), at.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
	}

	// A sidecar of any other shape fails the read rather than being taken
	// as no offset at all, which would hand back a plausible time.
	for _, raw := range []string{`"+03:30"`, `1.5`, `null`, `"12600"`} {
		if got, err := agtypeZone(map[string][]byte{"occurredAtOffset": []byte(raw)}, "occurredAtOffset", at); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeZone(%s) = %s, want an error", raw, got.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
		}
	}
}

// TestAgtypeZoneRefusesAnOffsetOutsideADay pins the bound on the
// sidecar. gqlc derives no sidecar to bind — a parameter crosses as the
// instant alone — so the integer the helper reads is whatever the graph
// holds: a query that names the key binds it like any other property,
// whether or not gqlc generated that query. Taken unchecked it lands
// the caller in a zone no clock keeps: 1000000000 seconds is 31 years
// east of UTC, and the wall clock read off it is decades from the
// instant stored beside it.
//
// A day either way, exclusive, is the bound, and both signs of it are
// pinned: an offset outside a day is refused on whichever side of UTC it
// falls.
func TestAgtypeZoneRefusesAnOffsetOutsideADay(t *testing.T) {
	at := instants[2].at

	// One second inside the bound at each edge. +23:59:59 belongs to no
	// zone a database holds today and is read here anyway: the admitted
	// set is a range, so a graph a future zone database would accept
	// survives this read.
	for _, offset := range []int{86399, -86399} {
		raw := strconv.Itoa(offset)
		got, err := agtypeZone(map[string][]byte{"occurredAtOffset": []byte(raw)}, "occurredAtOffset", at)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeZone(%s) = error %v, want the offset read", raw, err)
			continue
		}
		if _, off := got.Zone(); off != offset {
			t.Errorf("agtypeZone(%s) offset = %d seconds, want %d", raw, off, offset)
		}
	}

	// A whole day and beyond, at both signs. The int64 extremes are here
	// for the conversion the helper does after the check: int64 to int is
	// where a value this size stops being the number it was on a build
	// whose int is 32 bits.
	for _, offset := range []int64{86400, -86400, 1000000000, -1000000000, math.MaxInt64, math.MinInt64} {
		raw := strconv.FormatInt(offset, 10)
		got, err := agtypeZone(map[string][]byte{"occurredAtOffset": []byte(raw)}, "occurredAtOffset", at)
		if err == nil {
			_, off := got.Zone()
			t.Errorf("agtypeZone(%s) = %s at offset %d seconds, want an error", raw, got.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), off)
			continue
		}
		// A schema carries one sidecar per instant property, so the
		// number alone does not say which property of which vertex is
		// the malformed one.
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "occurredAtOffset") {
			t.Errorf("agtypeZone(%s) = error %v, which does not name the property it read", raw, err)
		}
	}
}

// Event vertices in the wire shape the captured texts above establish —
// jsonb key order, an absent key for a null — carrying the encoded
// instant and, beside it, the offset sidecar. Flat rather than nested,
// so the property a user's ORDER BY names is the integer itself.
const (
	eventPlain = `{"id": 1970324836974593, "label": "Event", "properties": {"id": 1, "occurredAt": 1704112496123456}}::vertex`
	eventZoned = `{"id": 1970324836974594, "label": "Event", "properties": {"id": 2, "occurredAt": 1704112496123456, "occurredAtOffset": 12600}}::vertex`
	eventSeen  = `{"id": 1970324836974595, "label": "Event", "properties": {"id": 3, "seenAt": 0, "occurredAt": 1704112496123456, "seenAtOffset": -18000}}::vertex`
)

func TestDecodeVertexReadsTheOffsetSidecarBesideItsInstant(t *testing.T) {
	want := instants[2].at

	plain, err := decodeEvent([]byte(eventPlain))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEvent(eventPlain) = error %v", err)
	}
	if !plain.OccurredAt.Equal(want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventPlain).OccurredAt = %s, want %s", plain.OccurredAt.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), want.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
	}
	if _, off := plain.OccurredAt.Zone(); off != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventPlain).OccurredAt is at offset %d, want UTC — no sidecar was stored", off)
	}
	if plain.SeenAt != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventPlain).SeenAt = %s, want nil", plain.SeenAt.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
	}

	// The sidecar is read from the vertex the instant came out of, under
	// the name the instant's own property name derives. Same moment, and
	// a wall clock 3.5 hours ahead of the UTC one.
	zoned, err := decodeEvent([]byte(eventZoned))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEvent(eventZoned) = error %v", err)
	}
	if !zoned.OccurredAt.Equal(want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventZoned).OccurredAt = %s, want the same instant %s",
			zoned.OccurredAt.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), want.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
	}
	if _, off := zoned.OccurredAt.Zone(); off != 12600 {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventZoned).OccurredAt is at offset %d seconds, want 12600", off)
	}
	if h, m, _ := zoned.OccurredAt.Clock(); h != 16 || m != 4 {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventZoned).OccurredAt reads %02d:%02d locally, want 16:04", h, m)
	}

	// The nullable arm zones too, and does it without disturbing the
	// absence a nil pointer carries.
	seen, err := decodeEvent([]byte(eventSeen))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEvent(eventSeen) = error %v", err)
	}
	if seen.SeenAt == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEvent(eventSeen).SeenAt = nil, want the epoch")
	}
	if !seen.SeenAt.Equal(instants[1].at) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventSeen).SeenAt = %s, want %s", seen.SeenAt.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), instants[1].at.Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
	}
	if _, off := seen.SeenAt.Zone(); off != -18000 {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(eventSeen).SeenAt is at offset %d seconds, want -18000", off)
	}

	// A sidecar the vertex holds under a shape no offset takes fails the
	// whole decode rather than yielding a vertex zoned by a guess.
	broken := strings.Replace(eventZoned, `"occurredAtOffset": 12600`, `"occurredAtOffset": "+03:30"`, 1)
	if got, err := decodeEvent([]byte(broken)); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEvent(broken sidecar) = %+v, want an error", got)
	}
}

// The emitted query method is the only place a bound instant is encoded,
// and the string it hands the driver is the whole of what AGE parses as
// the query's parameter map. Nothing about the encoding is visible in
// the method's Go signature, which takes and returns time.Time exactly
// as the neo4j targets do.
func TestEmittedMethodBindsAnInstantAsMicroseconds(t *testing.T) {
	seen := instants[1].at

	cases := []struct {
		name string
		arg  WriteEventParams
		want string
	}{
		{
			name: "an absent nullable instant is the agtype null",
			arg:  WriteEventParams{OccurredAt: instants[2].at, SeenAt: nil},
			want: `{"occurredAt":1704112496123456,"seenAt":null}`,
		},
		{
			name: "both instants cross as counts",
			arg:  WriteEventParams{OccurredAt: instants[2].at, SeenAt: &seen},
			want: `{"occurredAt":1704112496123456,"seenAt":0}`,
		},
		{
			name: "a zoned argument crosses as its instant",
			arg:  WriteEventParams{OccurredAt: tehran, SeenAt: nil},
			want: `{"occurredAt":1704112496123456,"seenAt":null}`,
		},
		{
			name: "a pre-epoch instant crosses negative",
			arg:  WriteEventParams{OccurredAt: instants[0].at, SeenAt: nil},
			want: `{"occurredAt":-14182940000000,"seenAt":null}`,
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		db := &recordingDB{}
		if err := (&Queries{db: db, graph: "corpus"}).WriteEvent(context.Background(), tc.arg); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: WriteEvent = error %v", tc.name, err)
			continue
		}
		if db.args != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: bound arguments =\n\t%s\nwant\n\t%s", tc.name, db.args, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// dates are the stored texts and the readings they mean, spanning the
// admitted range end to end. The two edges are the range itself: year 1
// day 1, and the last day of year 9999.
var dates = []struct {
	text string
	date Date
}{
	{"0001-01-01", Date{Year: 1, Month: 1, Day: 1}},
	{"1969-07-20", Date{Year: 1969, Month: 7, Day: 20}},
	{"2024-01-02", Date{Year: 2024, Month: 1, Day: 2}},
	{"2024-02-29", Date{Year: 2024, Month: 2, Day: 29}},
	{"9999-12-31", Date{Year: 9999, Month: 12, Day: 31}},
}

// TestAgtypeDateReadsTheStoredText reads each admitted text back, then
// re-encodes it. Encode and decode are one encoding read from either
// end, so a value surviving one and not the other is a defect neither
// direction sees alone.
func TestAgtypeDateReadsTheStoredText(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range dates {
		raw := []byte(`"` + tc.text + `"`)
		got, err := agtypeDate(raw)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDate(%s) = error %v, want %+v", raw, err, tc.date)
			continue
		}
		if got != tc.date {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDate(%s) = %+v, want %+v", raw, got, tc.date)
			continue
		}
		back, err := agtypeDateText(got)
		if err != nil || back != tc.text {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDateText(%+v) = %q, %v, want %q", got, back, err, tc.text)
		}
	}
}

// TestAgtypeDateRefusesTextThatWouldNotSortChronologically covers the
// three ways the stored text can be wrong, because they fail at three
// different places and a guard could be missing at any one of them: the
// text is not a date at all, or it is a real day spelled so that it sorts
// in the wrong place, or it is spelled correctly and lies outside the
// range the spelling orders.
//
// Year 0 is the row that makes the range check more than decoration. It
// is unsigned and four digits, so it parses and re-renders to itself and
// reaches the bound with both earlier guards satisfied. The rows one
// outside in the other direction never reach it — the layout reads four
// year digits and refuses a fifth, and refuses a sign — and they are here
// so that what refuses them is measured rather than assumed.
func TestAgtypeDateRefusesTextThatWouldNotSortChronologically(t *testing.T) {
	for _, raw := range []string{
		`"0000-01-01"`,
		`"0000-12-31"`,
		`"10000-01-01"`,
		`"-0001-01-01"`,
		`"2024-1-2"`,
		`"2024-01-2"`,
		`"24-01-02"`,
		`"2024-02-30"`,
		`"2024-13-01"`,
		`""`,
		`"not a date"`,
		`20240102`,
		`null`,
		`"2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"`,
	} {
		got, err := agtypeDate([]byte(raw))
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDate(%s) = %+v, want an error", raw, got)
			continue
		}
		if got != (Date{}) {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDate(%s) returned %+v alongside its error", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

// TestAgtypeDateTextRefusesADayOffTheCalendar is the encode half. The
// carrier is a plain struct of three ints, so nothing between the caller
// and the wire rejects February 30th but this: time.Date rolls it forward
// to March 2nd, and storing a different day than the caller wrote is the
// one failure the round trip above cannot catch.
func TestAgtypeDateTextRefusesADayOffTheCalendar(t *testing.T) {
	for _, d := range []Date{
		{Year: 0, Month: 1, Day: 1},
		{Year: -1, Month: 1, Day: 1},
		{Year: 10000, Month: 1, Day: 1},
		{Year: 2024, Month: 2, Day: 30},
		{Year: 2023, Month: 2, Day: 29},
		{Year: 2024, Month: 13, Day: 1},
		{Year: 2024, Month: 0, Day: 1},
		{Year: 2024, Month: 1, Day: 0},
		{Year: 2024, Month: 1, Day: 32},
		{},
	} {
		got, err := agtypeDateText(d)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDateText(%+v) = %q, want an error", d, got)
			continue
		}
		if got != "" {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDateText(%+v) returned %q alongside its error", d, got)
		}
	}
}

// localTimes are the stored counts and the readings they mean. The edges
// are midnight and the last microsecond before the next one.
var localTimes = []struct {
	micros int64
	at     LocalTime
}{
	{0, LocalTime{}},
	{3661000001, LocalTime{Hour: 1, Minute: 1, Second: 1, Nanosecond: 1000}},
	{43200000000, LocalTime{Hour: 12}},
	{86399999999, LocalTime{Hour: 23, Minute: 59, Second: 59, Nanosecond: 999999000}},
}

func TestAgtypeLocalTimeCountsMicrosecondsFromMidnight(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range localTimes {
		raw := strconv.FormatInt(tc.micros, 10)
		got, err := agtypeLocalTime([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeLocalTime(%s) = error %v, want %+v", raw, err, tc.at)
			continue
		}
		if got != tc.at {
			t.Errorf("agtypeLocalTime(%s) = %+v, want %+v", raw, got, tc.at)
			continue
		}
		back, err := agtypeLocalTimeMicros(got)
		if err != nil || back != tc.micros {
			t.Errorf("agtypeLocalTimeMicros(%+v) = %d, %v, want %d", got, back, err, tc.micros)
		}
	}
}

// TestAgtypeLocalTimeRefusesACountOutsideTheDay bounds the stored count
// at both ends. The one-microsecond rows are what a bound written with
// the wrong comparison lets through — 86400000000 is midnight tomorrow,
// which is a reading of the day after the one the column holds — and the
// int64 extremes are what an absent bound lets through.
func TestAgtypeLocalTimeRefusesACountOutsideTheDay(t *testing.T) {
	for _, micros := range []int64{-1, 86400000000, 86400000001, math.MaxInt64, math.MinInt64} {
		raw := strconv.FormatInt(micros, 10)
		got, err := agtypeLocalTime([]byte(raw))
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeLocalTime(%s) = %+v, want an error", raw, got)
			continue
		}
		// The count is the whole of what went wrong, so it has to be in
		// the message: a reader looking at a failed row has the property
		// name from the decoder that called this and nothing else.
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), raw) {
			t.Errorf("agtypeLocalTime(%s) = error %v, which does not name the count it read", raw, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestAgtypeLocalTimeMicrosRefusesAReadingOffTheClock is the encode half,
// and it is not the same check read backwards. Each component is bounded
// on its own, so an hour of -1 beside a minute of 60 is refused even
// though the two sum to midnight, which is inside the interval the decode
// enforces. That row is the one a single interval check lets through.
func TestAgtypeLocalTimeMicrosRefusesAReadingOffTheClock(t *testing.T) {
	for _, at := range []LocalTime{
		{Hour: -1, Minute: 60},
		{Hour: 24},
		{Hour: -1},
		{Minute: 60},
		{Minute: -1},
		{Second: 60},
		{Second: -1},
		{Nanosecond: 1000000000},
		{Nanosecond: -1},
	} {
		got, err := agtypeLocalTimeMicros(at)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeLocalTimeMicros(%+v) = %d, want an error", at, got)
			continue
		}
		if got != 0 {
			t.Errorf("agtypeLocalTimeMicros(%+v) returned %d alongside its error", at, got)
		}
	}
}

// durations are the stored counts and the durations they mean. What the
// decode returns is normalised — one stored number cannot fill Months and
// Days as well — so these are the encodings of the NORMALISED value, and
// the round trip below starts from that rather than from what a caller
// might have written.
var durations = []struct {
	micros int64
	d      Duration
}{
	{0, Duration{}},
	{1, Duration{Nanos: 1000}},
	{90000000, Duration{Seconds: 90}},
	{-90000000, Duration{Seconds: -90}},
	{7776000000000, Duration{Seconds: 7776000}},
}

func TestAgtypeDurationCountsTotalMicroseconds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range durations {
		raw := strconv.FormatInt(tc.micros, 10)
		got, err := agtypeDuration([]byte(raw))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDuration(%s) = error %v, want %+v", raw, err, tc.d)
			continue
		}
		if got != tc.d {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDuration(%s) = %+v, want %+v", raw, got, tc.d)
			continue
		}
		back, err := agtypeDurationMicros(got)
		if err != nil || back != tc.micros {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDurationMicros(%+v) = %d, %v, want %d", got, back, err, tc.micros)
		}
	}
}

// TestAgtypeDurationMicrosFoldsDaysAndRefusesMonths pins the one place
// the two calendar fields are treated differently, which is the whole of
// what makes this encoding lossless where it is admitted.
//
// A day folds: it is 86400 seconds here, in an encoding that carries no
// zone and so has no daylight-saving transition to land on. A month does
// not: it is 28, 29, 30 or 31 days depending on where it falls, so every
// count this could return is one the caller did not write, and a
// comparison against it would be answered wrongly rather than refused.
func TestAgtypeDurationMicrosFoldsDaysAndRefusesMonths(t *testing.T) {
	folds := []struct {
		d    Duration
		want int64
	}{
		{Duration{Days: 1}, 86400000000},
		{Duration{Days: 90}, 7776000000000},
		{Duration{Days: -1}, -86400000000},
		{Duration{Days: 1, Seconds: 1, Nanos: 1000}, 86401000001},
		{Duration{Nanos: 999}, 0},
	}
	for _, tc := range folds {
		got, err := agtypeDurationMicros(tc.d)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDurationMicros(%+v) = error %v, want %d", tc.d, err, tc.want)
			continue
		}
		if got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDurationMicros(%+v) = %d, want %d", tc.d, got, tc.want)
		}
	}

	for _, d := range []Duration{
		{Months: 1},
		{Months: -1},
		{Months: 12},
		{Months: 1, Days: 1, Seconds: 1},
	} {
		got, err := agtypeDurationMicros(d)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDurationMicros(%+v) = %d, want an error", d, got)
			continue
		}
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "month") {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDurationMicros(%+v) = error %v, which does not say months are what it refused", d, err)
		}
		if got != 0 {
			t.Errorf("agtypeDurationMicros(%+v) returned %d alongside its error", d, got)
		}
	}
}

// TestEmittedMethodBindsTheCarriersAsTheirScalars runs the emitted query
// method, which is the only place a bound DATE, LOCAL TIME or DURATION is
// encoded. Nothing about any of the three encodings is visible in the
// method's Go signature: it takes the same neutral carriers every backend
// takes, and what separates them is entirely in the bytes below.
//
// The refusal rows are the half a golden comparison cannot reach. These
// encoders fail, unlike the instant's, so the emission has to run them
// before it builds the argument map and return what they say — and a
// method that swallowed the error would still emit a plausible statement.
func TestEmittedMethodBindsTheCarriersAsTheirScalars(t *testing.T) {
	ends := Date{Year: 9999, Month: 12, Day: 31}

	cases := []struct {
		name string
		arg  WriteSpanParams
		want string
	}{
		{
			name: "an absent nullable date is the agtype null",
			arg: WriteSpanParams{
				StartsOn: Date{Year: 2024, Month: 1, Day: 2},
				OpensAt:  LocalTime{Hour: 1},
				Lasts:    Duration{Seconds: 90},
			},
			want: `{"endsOn":null,"lasts":90000000,"opensAt":3600000000,"startsOn":"2024-01-02"}`,
		},
		{
			name: "each carrier crosses as its own scalar",
			arg: WriteSpanParams{
				StartsOn: Date{Year: 1, Month: 1, Day: 1},
				EndsOn:   &ends,
				OpensAt:  LocalTime{Hour: 23, Minute: 59, Second: 59, Nanosecond: 999999000},
				Lasts:    Duration{Days: 1, Seconds: 1},
			},
			want: `{"endsOn":"9999-12-31","lasts":86401000000,"opensAt":86399999999,"startsOn":"0001-01-01"}`,
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		db := &recordingDB{}
		if err := (&Queries{db: db, graph: "corpus"}).WriteSpan(context.Background(), tc.arg); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: WriteSpan = error %v", tc.name, err)
			continue
		}
		if db.args != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: bound arguments =\n\t%s\nwant\n\t%s", tc.name, db.args, tc.want)
		}
	}

	// One refusal per encoder, plus one reached through the nullable
	// combinator, because each is a separate call site in the emitted
	// method and one of them could be missing its error check.
	badEnds := Date{Year: 10000, Month: 1, Day: 1}
	refusals := []struct {
		name  string
		arg   WriteSpanParams
		names string
	}{
		{
			name:  "a date off the calendar",
			arg:   WriteSpanParams{StartsOn: Date{Year: 2024, Month: 2, Day: 30}},
			names: "startsOn",
		},
		{
			name:  "a present nullable date off the calendar",
			arg:   WriteSpanParams{StartsOn: Date{Year: 2024, Month: 1, Day: 2}, EndsOn: &badEnds},
			names: "endsOn",
		},
		{
			name: "a reading off the clock",
			arg: WriteSpanParams{
				StartsOn: Date{Year: 2024, Month: 1, Day: 2},
				OpensAt:  LocalTime{Hour: 24},
			},
			names: "opensAt",
		},
		{
			name: "a duration carrying months",
			arg: WriteSpanParams{
				StartsOn: Date{Year: 2024, Month: 1, Day: 2},
				Lasts:    Duration{Months: 1},
			},
			names: "lasts",
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range refusals {
		db := &recordingDB{}
		err := (&Queries{db: db, graph: "corpus"}).WriteSpan(context.Background(), tc.arg)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: WriteSpan = nil, want an error", tc.name)
			continue
		}
		// The parameter name is what tells the caller which of four
		// arguments to fix; without it the message names an encoding they
		// did not write and cannot locate.
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.names) {
			t.Errorf("%s: WriteSpan = error %v, which does not name parameter $%s", tc.name, err, tc.names)
		}
		if db.args != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: WriteSpan sent %s despite refusing the argument", tc.name, db.args)
		}
	}
}

func TestBoundGraphCountsBytes(t *testing.T) {
	// 63 is PostgreSQL's name capacity in BYTES, so the boundary a
	// multi-byte name crosses is not the one its character count
	// suggests: 32 two-byte characters is 64 bytes and over the limit
	// while 63 one-byte characters is exactly at it.
	cases := map[string]struct {
		graph string
		want  bool
	}{
		"empty":                {"", true},
		"ascii at the limit":   {strings.Repeat("a", 63), true},
		"ascii over by one":    {strings.Repeat("a", 64), false},
		"two-byte at the limit": {strings.Repeat("é", 31) + "a", true},
		"two-byte over by one": {strings.Repeat("é", 32), false},
		"characters under, bytes over": {strings.Repeat("é", 40), false},
		"three-byte over":      {strings.Repeat("中", 22), false},
	}
	for name, tc := range cases {
		got, err := (&Queries{graph: tc.graph}).boundGraph()
		if tc.want {
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("%s: boundGraph() = error %v, want the name back", name, err)
			} else if got != tc.graph {
				t.Errorf("%s: boundGraph() = %q, want %q", name, got, tc.graph)
			}
			continue
		}
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: boundGraph() = %q, want an error", name, got)
			continue
		}
		if got != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: boundGraph() returned %q alongside its error", name, got)
		}
	}
}
